title: Distance, kNN & Clustering
why: Similarity is the idea behind recommendations, search and segmentation, and top-k selection is a classic coding-interview pattern.
explain: Many methods rest on distance. k-nearest neighbors (kNN) classifies a point by a vote among its k closest training points. k-means groups points into k clusters by alternating two steps: assign each point to its nearest centroid, then move each centroid to the mean of its points, until assignments stop changing.

The distance you choose matters. Euclidean distance is sensitive to feature scale, so standardize first; cosine distance ignores magnitude and suits text and embeddings; Manhattan distance is more robust to outliers. In high dimensions distances concentrate (the curse of dimensionality), so nearest neighbors become less meaningful.

k-means needs k chosen (use the elbow on inertia or the silhouette score), is sensitive to initialization (use k-means++), and assumes roughly round clusters of similar size. A clustering is only useful if the segments are stable and actionable.
key_points: kNN has no training step; all cost is paid at prediction time
k-means alternates assign and update; it converges to a local optimum
Standardize features before using Euclidean distance
Choose k with elbow and silhouette, then sanity-check with domain sense
k-means++ initialization reduces bad local optima
pitfalls: One large-scale feature dominating the distance
Reporting clusters without checking stability across random seeds

leetcode.why: Finding the k closest points is the kNN query; do it with a heap.
Quickselect and heaps find the k-th element without a full sort, the trick behind efficient neighbor search.
Connected components via union-find or DFS is graph-based clustering.
Flood-filling grid regions is the same idea as connected-component clustering on pixels.
Merging k sorted lists with a heap is how sharded nearest-neighbor results get combined.

industry.q: How do you choose k in k-means?
key_points: Plot inertia against k and look for the elbow
Silhouette score for cohesion vs separation

industry.q: kNN prediction is too slow on 10 million points. How do you speed it up?
key_points: KD-tree or ball tree work in low dimensions
Approximate nearest neighbor indexes (HNSW, IVF, LSH) in high dimensions

industry.q: Your clusters are dominated by one feature with a huge scale. Diagnose and fix it.
key_points: Consider feature weighting or dropping redundant features
Re-evaluate with silhouette after the change
